# Refactor skill: REFACTOR markers cross-wired and added without a fix

**Headline:** The 2026-11-06 scheduled `/skill:refactor` run wrote
`REFACTOR-<id>` markers whose work-item id belonged to a *different* file, and
wrote them into files it never changed. The positional mis-pairing itself is
already fixed in code (identity-keyed mapping, b05cbad554 /
SA-0MWE1E4GQ004E1JG), but nothing pins that fix and nothing stops a future
mis-pairing from reaching disk. This item adds the missing regression coverage,
a fail-closed identity check before a marker is written, and a marker block
that states the smell is pre-existing and unfixed.

## Problem statement

A scheduled full-project refactor run injected marker-only edits into files the
run had not changed, carrying ids of work items that named *other* files; the
genuine mechanical fixes landed elsewhere with no marker at all. Release prep
had to revert the two marker-only hunks (b536b9dbe) before the tree could be
shipped, and the mismatch made the scan report untrustworthy.

## Users

- **Producers running `/skill:refactor`** (directly or via the scheduler) — they
  read the injected markers as "this file still carries tracked debt"; a
  cross-wired marker sends them to the wrong file.
- **Implementation agents** working a refactor item — they trust the marker in
  the file named by the item, and are misled when the marker names a foreign
  item or the item's own file carries no marker.
- **Release/prep agents** — marker-only hunks with no accompanying fix are
  indistinguishable from real changes and block or churn a release.

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when a refactor run annotates a file, I want the marker's work
  item to name exactly that file, so that following the marker leads me to the
  right fix."
- "As a release agent, when I see a marker-only diff, I want the marker itself
  to say the smell is pre-existing and unfixed, so that I do not treat the hunk
  as an attempted fix that failed."

## Acceptance Criteria

- A pipeline-level regression test exercises `remediate_pre_existing()` with a
  smell batch shaped like the 2026-11-06 incident (one identity group skipped or
  collapsed to `None` before a later group's injection) and fails on the
  positional-index implementation: every injected `REFACTOR-<id>` marker must
  carry the id the batch filed for *that* smell's finding identity, and no
  marker may be written outside the file its work item names.
- Marker injection is fail-closed on identity: before writing, the resolved
  work item's identity (its `Refactor-Finding-Key` when present, otherwise the
  file path recorded in its title/description) is compared with the smell's
  `<code>:<repository-relative path>`; a mismatch writes nothing, logs a
  warning, and increments a mismatch counter surfaced in both the JSON report
  and the human-readable scan summary.
- A legacy item without a `Refactor-Finding-Key` marker (e.g. one whose
  description was rewritten by intake) still receives its marker through the
  title/description path fallback, so verification never silently drops a
  correctly paired marker.
- The injected marker block states that the smell is pre-existing and unfixed
  (an additive `state:` line), so a marker-only edit documents why it
  accompanies no code change; the existing parsers (`REFACTOR_PATTERN`,
  `REFACTOR_COMMENT_PATTERN`, `has_existing_smell_comment`) and the planned
  stale-marker removal sweep still match the block.
- Unit tests cover the identity-verification helper (matching item, mismatched
  item, legacy item without a marker, absent item) and parser compatibility of
  the new `state:` line.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` (marker block format, verification
  behaviour, cross-wiring failure mode), and any relevant wiki or docs site
  entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A refactor run can only annotate the file its work item names, and every marker
it leaves behind says plainly that the smell is pre-existing and unfixed — so a
marker-only diff can no longer be mistaken for a fix or land in the wrong file.

## Constraints

- No retroactive edits to history: the two reverted hunks (b536b9dbe) stay
  reverted; no existing marker in the tree is rewritten by this item.
- The `state:` line must be additive — the marker's first line stays
  `REFACTOR-<id>` and the `smell:` line stays in its current position, so
  removal/sweep tooling (SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9, SA-0MWFW1ZDT006VYM4) and the
  two existing regexes keep working.
- Verification must be cheap: at most one extra `wl show`/`wl list` lookup per
  injected marker, and no new dependency on network or LLM calls.
- No behaviour change to auto-fix, smell detection, or item creation; only the
  marker-write path and its reporting change.
- The canonical source is this repository (`skill/refactor/`); the installed
  copy under `~/.pi/agent/skills/refactor` is a symlink and is never edited.
- All work-item bookkeeping uses `wl`; no edits to
  `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl`.
- Test execution goes through `/skill:test` (never ad-hoc pytest).

## Existing state

- **Root cause (already fixed):** before b05cbad554 (`SA-0MWE1E4GQ004E1JG`,
  "Machine-readable finding identity marker", landed 2026-11-13),
  `remediate_pre_existing()` paired work-item ids to smells **positionally**:
  `smell_index = smells.index(smell); created_ids[smell_index]`. Because
  `create_smell_work_items()` omits skipped/failed groups, any skip shifted
  every later pairing by one. On 2026-11-06 (`22:06`) that produced exactly the
  observed cross-wiring: `skill/implement/tests/test_cleanup_worktree_action.py`
  received `REFACTOR-SA-0MW5IZN330071FQU` (the item for
  `tests/test_implement_drive_worktree_cleanup.py`) and
  `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_green_run.py` received
  `REFACTOR-SA-0MW5IZLES00362FK` (the item for
  `skill/implement/tests/test_cleanup_worktree_action.py`).
- The fix replaced positional pairing with
  `create_smell_work_items_mapped()` + `created_map.get(build_finding_key(smell))`
  (`skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py`, `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py`).
- **No test pins the pairing.** Nothing under `tests/test_refactor/` references
  `create_smell_work_items_mapped`; `remediate_pre_existing` is only mocked in
  `tests/test_refactor/test_auto_fix.py`. A regression to positional pairing
  would pass the current suite.
- `inject_refactor_comment()` (`skill/refactor/comment_injection.py`) writes the
  block at the file head (below a shebang) after only a duplicate-by-smell-type
  check; it never verifies that `work_item_id` actually tracks this file, so a
  wrong id is written silently.
- The block content is `REFACTOR-<id>` / `smell:` / `severity:` /
  `description:` with no statement about fix state, which is why a marker-only
  hunk reads like an attempted fix.
- Legacy refactor items whose descriptions were rewritten (e.g.
  `SA-0MWI3MT6L004K1L7`) do not carry `Refactor-Finding-Key`; its own
  OPEN QUESTION records that gap. Verification therefore cannot rely on the
  marker alone.

## Desired change

- Extract the identity resolution used by `_find_existing_worklog_item` so the
  injection path can resolve an item's identity in one place (marker first,
  title/description file-path fallback second).
- In `remediate_pre_existing()`, verify the pairing before calling
  `inject_refactor_comment()`; on mismatch skip the write, log, and count it in
  a new `comment_identity_mismatches` field in the report dict.
- Add the `state: pre-existing, not fixed` line to `_build_comment_block()`
  output (both block and line-prefixed styles) and assert parser compatibility.
- Add `tests/test_refactor/test_marker_pairing.py` (name indicative) with the
  incident-shaped regression test plus verification-helper unit tests.
- Document the marker block, the verification step and the cross-wiring failure
  mode in `skill/refactor/SKILL.md`.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — `remediate_pre_existing()`: identity
  verification before injection, mismatch counter in the report dict.
- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` — `_build_comment_block()`: additive
  `state:` line; `inject_refactor_comment()`: identity-guard hook.
- `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — shared helper that resolves a work
  item's finding identity (marker or path fallback), reused by the guard.
- `tests/test_refactor/test_marker_pairing.py` — new pipeline-level
  cross-wiring regression tests.
- `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` — `state:` line and parser
  compatibility tests.
- `tests/test_refactor/test_workitem_creation.py` — identity-resolution unit
  tests (marker, legacy fallback, absent).
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — marker block format, verification, failure mode.

## Related work

- `SA-0MWE1E4GQ004E1JG` (completed) — introduced the identity marker and the
  identity-keyed mapping that already fixes the positional mis-pairing. This
  item adds the regression coverage and the write-time guard it left out.
- `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9` (open) — removes stale `REFACTOR` markers when their
  work item closes; the `state:` line must stay compatible with its parser.
- `SA-0MVVF468O009TAIF` (open) — marker placement relative to shebang/encoding
  line/docstring; same write path, so ordering must be agreed but not re-solved
  here.
- `SA-0MVNBEPHH009LB5X` (open) — the report claims unfixed diagnostics as
  auto-fixes; complementary trust defect in the same report.
- `SA-0MVZHMZBU005FEJN` (open) — `remediate_pre_existing()` drops skipped
  findings silently inside the same `comment_errors` counter; the new
  `comment_identity_mismatches` counter must compose with that item's
  per-finding skip reasons rather than duplicate them.
- `SA-0MW7Z1JCE009G6J3` (open) — re-verification of linter-derived items
  (consumes `Refactor-Fingerprint`).
- `SA-0MVZA21600087VRD`, `SA-0MWFW20O2008AG91`, `SA-0MWFW2389003HHVE` (open /
  blocked) — marker sweep family; parsers must stay compatible.
- `SA-0MWI3MT6L004K1L7` (open) — example legacy item with no
  `Refactor-Finding-Key`; motivates the path fallback.
- Discovery record: `SA-0MW5KI5FH004OK7O` (completed) — release prep that
  reverted the cross-wired marker-only hunks in b536b9dbe.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (recorded, producer to confirm):** the second expectation
  ("a marker must only accompany an actual fix, or explicitly document why no
  fix is applied") is satisfied by the additive `state: pre-existing, not
  fixed` line rather than by suppressing markers for unfixed smells — markers
  exist to track *unfixed* pre-existing debt, so suppressing them would remove
  the skill's dedupe signal. See Appendix Q1.
- **Risk:** a strict verification guard could skip legacy items en masse. The
  path fallback plus a reported (not silent) mismatch count mitigates this;
  the mismatch counter makes any systematic skip visible in the scan report.
- **Risk of scope creep:** the marker lifecycle (removal, re-verification,
  placement) has four sibling items; this item must not absorb them.
- **Risk:** an extra `wl show` per marker could slow full-project scans;
  mitigated by resolving identity once per group rather than per smell, and by
  keeping the guard subprocess count bounded.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (OPEN QUESTION — producer decision required).** The item's second
  expectation reads "a marker must only accompany an actual fix (or explicitly
  document why no fix is applied)". Markers are injected for *pre-existing,
  unfixed* smells by design, so which reading applies?
  - (a) Keep injecting markers for unfixed smells, and have the block state
    `state: pre-existing, not fixed` so a marker-only hunk is self-documenting.
  - (b) Stop injecting markers into files the run did not modify (markers only
    for session-scoped scans or only for files the auto-fix step touched).
  - (c) Keep markers as-is and rely on the run report/commit message to state
    that the markers accompany no fix.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — smallest behavioural change, keeps the dedupe signal
    that marker presence provides, and satisfies "explicitly document why no
    fix is applied" in the marker itself. Research: design intent recorded in
    `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` ("Inject structured REFACTOR
    comments into source files to track pre-existing…") and
    `skill/refactor/SKILL.md`; (b) would silently remove duplicate suppression
    for every full-project scan.
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — recorded 2026-11-17 by the intake agent; no
    producer response yet. The brief and ACs proceed on the recommended option
    (a) so implementation is not blocked, and option (b) is reachable by
    dropping AC4 and gating injection on the modified-file set.
- **Q2.** Is the identity-keyed mapping from b05cbad554
  (`SA-0MWE1E4GQ004E1JG`) accepted as the root-cause fix, so this item carries
  only regression coverage plus the write-time guard?
  - Answer (agent, from repository evidence): yes — `git show b05cbad554` shows
    the positional `smells.index(smell)` pairing being replaced by
    `created_map.get(build_finding_key(smell))`, and `SA-0MWE1E4GQ004E1JG` is
    `completed`/`done`. This item therefore adds tests and defence-in-depth
    rather than a second root-cause fix. Source: `git show b05cbad554`,
    `wl show SA-0MWE1E4GQ004E1JG --json`.
- **Q3.** Should marker verification be fail-closed (skip and report) or
  fail-open (write and warn) when the target item's identity cannot be
  resolved?
  - Answer (agent, from repository evidence): fail-closed — the defect under
    repair is a *wrong* marker reaching disk, and a skipped marker is
    recoverable (the item still exists and the next scan re-finds the smell),
    while a cross-wired marker misleads readers. Migration safety is preserved
    by the legacy path fallback and the reported mismatch count. Source:
    "Expected" section of the seed description; existing fail-open precedent in
    `_find_existing_worklog_item` applies to *detection*, not to writes.
- **Duplicate-work check:** `wl search "REFACTOR marker" --json` and
  `wl search "Refactor-Finding-Key" --json` returned no item covering marker /
  item pairing tests or write-time identity verification; the only overlapping
  item (`SA-0MWE1E4GQ004E1JG`) fixed the root cause and is completed, and the
  removal/placement family (SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9, SA-0MVVF468O009TAIF,
  SA-0MVZA21600087VRD) is explicitly out of scope here.
- **Session:** intake run by `Map` on 2026-11-17 for
  `SA-0MW5KKEHL005BR0L`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVZHMZBU005FEJN** – Refactor step discards pre-existing smell findings silently (5 comment_errors, 0 work items created) (open)
- **SA-0MRIIQLQI001RQVB** – Refactor command/doc.md for conciseness (completed)
- **SA-0MQPP6TFJ008LU1N** – wl close: add recovery path for done parent with open children (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: absent, absorb, ac4, acceptance, accepted (+410 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mwe1e4gq004e1jg, absent, absorb, ac4, acceptance (+410 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: absent, absorb, ac4, acceptance, accepted (+403 more)

# Intake Brief — Audit runner leaves stale `pending-screens.json` when no child screens remain

## Problem statement

The audit runner clears its in-memory view of pending child screens but does **not** delete (or empty) the on-disk `<issue_id>.pending-screens.json` signal when the collected pending set for a run is empty. Because `cmd_issue` bypasses the freshness fast-path while that file names any child, a stale signal forces every later audit of the item to re-run the whole Phase 1 pipeline (one model call each) even though nothing is pending — a silent, repeatable cost that contradicts the documented "cleared automatically once none remain" contract.

## Users

- **Operators/agents auditing a parent item** whose child screens were already resolved (child closed as duplicate, fixed upstream, or serviced in a prior run) — they re-audit an item that is genuinely settled and unexpectedly pay for a full pipeline run each time.
- **The herdr downtime dispatcher** — dispatch-driven audits inherit the same wasted-cost path when a signal lingers.
- **Maintainers reading the audit docs** — the documented resume/clear contract currently overstates actual behaviour.

Example user stories:

- As an operator re-auditing `CG-0MW917K7V009LMLE` after closing its only child, I want the stale signal removed so the next audit takes the freshness fast-path instead of re-running Phase 1.
- As a maintainer, I want a closed child to never be persisted into the pending-screens signal, so the signal can only ever name screens that can still be serviced.

## Observed behaviour (reproduction)

Observed on 2026-11-09 auditing `CG-0MW917K7V009LMLE` (Tableau-Card-Engine):

1. Run 1 (default in-main-slot mode) emitted one child screen for `CG-0MW97UZ68001JTGK` and wrote `.worklog/audit-checkpoints/CG-0MW917K7V009LMLE.pending-screens.json`.
2. The child was then closed (duplicate; failure fixed upstream).
3. Resume run reported `"pending_child_screens": []` and a `Ready to close: Yes` verdict, **but the signal file remained**, still naming the closed child.
4. Workaround applied at the time: the stale file was deleted by hand so the next audit could take the freshness fast-path.

## Existing state / root cause (verified in tree)

The signal write and the reported pending set are derived from **two different predicates**, so they can disagree:

- The `--json` payload / readiness gate computes `pending_child_screens` as `_pending_main_slot_child_ids(child_results)` **minus** `_unserviced_main_slot_child_ids(child_results, stale_pending_ids)` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` ~`:10540`).
- The signal write at the report-assembly site calls `_write_pending_screens_signal(_pending_main_slot_child_ids(child_results), …)` — **unfiltered** (`:16747`–`:16756`). `_write_pending_screens_signal` does unlink when it receives an empty list (`:8005`), so it only stays stale when it receives a non-empty list.
- On a checkpoint resume, `active_children` excludes only `deleted` (`:15641`), so a child closed as `completed`/`done` **stays** in the restored `child_results` still carrying the `partial` + `main-session review` pending marker. `_re_resolve_pending_main_slot_children` cannot re-resolve a closed-as-duplicate child (no own stored audit), so it is left carrying the placeholder (`:15526`).
- Net effect: the closed child is subtracted from the reported `pending_child_screens` (it is "unserviced", `:10542`) yet re-written into the signal (unfiltered, `:16753`) — exactly the observed "JSON says `[]`, file still names the child".

Secondary path worth covering: any early-return / short-circuit that never reaches the report-assembly write (freshness fast-path at `:13364`–`:13377`, dry-run freshness refresh guard at `:17593`) also leaves an existing stale file untouched.

Documented contract it violates: `skill/audit/SKILL.md:233` and `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md:1226` both state the signal "is cleared/deleted automatically once none remain".

## Desired change

Make the on-disk signal a faithful mirror of the screens that can still be serviced:

1. Derive **both** the reported `pending_child_screens` and the signal contents from a **single** shared helper so they cannot diverge.
2. A child that is closed (`status=completed`/`stage=done`) or `deleted` must **never** be persisted into the signal — it can never be serviced by a later run.
3. When the resulting signal set is empty, the file is removed (existing `unlink(missing_ok=True)` path) on **both** the fresh-run and resume paths, including the short-circuit paths that currently skip the write.
4. Genuinely outstanding screens are unchanged: an **open**, unserviced child still keeps the signal (and therefore the freshness-gate bypass + resume behaviour).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: When the collected pending set for a run is empty, `<issue_id>.pending-screens.json` is removed from the checkpoint directory on both the fresh-run and the resume path — the file does not survive a run whose JSON payload reports `"pending_child_screens": []`.
- AC2: A child that is closed (`status=completed`/`stage=done`) or `deleted` is never written into the signal; the signal only ever names children whose screens can still be serviced.
- AC3: Genuinely pending screens are unaffected — with an open, unserviced child still outstanding, the signal survives and still lists that child, and the freshness-gate bypass / checkpoint-resume contract still collects a serviced child with zero child `pi` calls.
- AC4 (validation): Regression tests prove (a) resume with the named child closed ⇒ signal removed and payload `pending_child_screens == []`; (b) fresh run with a closed child ⇒ no signal written; (c) control: an open unserviced child ⇒ signal present and naming that child. Tests exercise the real `_write_pending_screens_signal` / report-assembly path with `wl`/`pi` mocked (no real subprocess, no self-referential re-implementation of game/audit logic).
- AC5: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries — stating precisely when the signal is cleared and which children it can name.
- AC6: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Operators re-auditing a parent whose child screens are already resolved stop paying for a full Phase 1 re-run on every audit, because a resolved child can no longer leave a signal that permanently bypasses the freshness fast-path.

## Constraints

- Surgical change confined to the audit runner's signal derivation; no behaviour change for genuinely outstanding screens (AC3).
- Do **not** fix this by subtracting every `_unserviced_main_slot_child_ids` entry — that would clear the signal for genuinely unserviced *open* children, re-clamping the item on the freshness fast-path and losing the resume.
- `--no-checkpoint` behaviour is unchanged (it reads/writes no signal).
- Manual deletion of stale files is the existing workaround, not the fix.
- Bulk sweeping of already-stale signals across project worklogs is out of scope (tracked by SA-0MW2J8FDB004VDRS).
- UK English in all written output.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** a closed (`completed`/`done`) or `deleted` child can never need an in-main-slot screen, so it must never appear in the signal. Implementation should confirm against the production case (child closed as duplicate).
- **Risk — over-clearing:** naively subtracting all unserviced ids clears signals for open unserviced children. Mitigation: drop only children that can never be serviced (closed/deleted) or are provably resolved; keep the helper's identity test explicit.
- **Risk — re-divergence:** two predicates is the bug class. Mitigation: one helper feeds both the report/JSON set and the signal set (AC1/AC2).
- **Risk — scope creep:** the 43-signal cross-project sweep belongs to SA-0MW2J8FDB004VDRS; record any extra opportunity as a linked item, not scope here.
- **Assumption:** the send/clear contract stays "signal names only serviceable screens", so the docs are corrected to match tightened behaviour rather than rewritten.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_pending_main_slot_child_ids` (~:7960), `_write_pending_screens_signal` (~:7984), `_is_unserviced_main_slot_child` (~:8028), `_unserviced_main_slot_child_ids` (~:8119), `_read_pending_screens_signal` (~:8182); call site ~:16747–:16756; reported `pending_child_screens` ~:10540; freshness fast-path ~:13364–:13377; dry-run refresh guard ~:17593.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` — extend the existing resume-clears-signal coverage (`test_resume_then_report_clears_gate_and_signal` ~:1300, `_write_signal` helper ~:407) with the closed-child case and the open-child control.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (:233) — child-audit execution contract wording.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (:1226) — resumable-signal contract wording.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S** (completed) — in-main-slot child-screen resume (D1 freshness gate + D2 checkpoint replay); the resume cycle this bug sits on top of.
- **SA-0MU32TE120012T49** (completed) — introduced the resumable pending-screens signal and the "cleared automatically when none remain" contract.
- **SA-0MVAWFUU0004VW45** (completed) — unserviced in-main-slot verdict handling; source of the `unserviced_ids` subtraction that the signal write omits.
- **SA-0MW2J7O3D0044SFM** (completed) — re-resolve pending children on checkpoint resume; the reconcile path that cannot re-resolve a closed child.
- **SA-0MW2J7NGP006CIEG** (completed) — made the freshness gate pending-screens aware (the bypass a stale file keeps triggering).
- **SA-0MW2J8FDB004VDRS** (open) — one-off operational sweep of stale signals; explicitly defers the root-cause guard to this item.
- **SA-0MW2J8G260045D17** (open) — dispatched audits should not emit unserviceable screens; adjacent (a dispatched audit produces exactly the unserviced state this signal bug then pins).

Automated find-related report (`find-related`): related work items SA-0MW2J7O3D0044SFM, SA-0MU32TE120012T49, SA-0MW2J8FDB004VDRS; repository matches `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (plus a loose `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` match, not relevant). Full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-SA-0MW9B11HE003AZZU.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Note:** the seed context was complete — problem, impact, reproduction, expected vs actual, and the manual workaround were all supplied — and the root cause was confirmed by reading the tree. No requirement-discovery interview was needed; the entries below record the research that stood in for it.

- **Q (self-resolved by repo research): where does the signal get written?** Answer: `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` `_write_pending_screens_signal` (~:7984), called once at report assembly (~:16752) with the **unfiltered** `_pending_main_slot_child_ids(child_results)`. Evidence: `grep -n "_write_pending_screens_signal"` → definition + single call site.
- **Q: why does the payload report `[]` while the file persists?** Answer: the payload subtracts `unserviced_ids` (~:10540–:10543) but the signal write does not (~:16753); a closed-as-duplicate child stays in restored `child_results` with the pending marker and is classified unserviced. Evidence: tree read of `_unserviced_main_slot_child_ids` (~:8119), `_re_resolve_pending_main_slot_children` (~:15505) and `active_children` filter (~:15641).
- **Q: is this a duplicate of the sweep item?** Answer: no — SA-0MW2J8FDB004VDRS is an operational sweep and states "the root-cause guard against stale leftovers is SA-0MW9B11HE003AZZU and stays out of scope here." Evidence: `wl show SA-0MW2J8FDB004VDRS --json` constraints section.
- **Q: does a documented contract need changing?** Answer: no — both docs already state the signal is "cleared automatically once none remain"; the implementation diverges, so the docs need precision (which children may be named), not a behaviour change. Evidence: `skill/audit/SKILL.md:233`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md:1226`.

# Stage-aware unified hang diagnostic builder

**Parent:** SA-0MWEURUYL004I470 — Release gate: stage-aware hang diagnostics + hybrid load-aware unit-stage bound
**Slice type:** feature (tracer bullet: diagnostic end-to-end — code, tests, header comment)
**Parent ACs covered:** AC1, AC2

## Goal

As a release producer whose gate aborted in the unit stage, I want one `[hang-timeout]` block
that tells me the stage, the configured bound, the elapsed time, how far over the bound the
stage ran and what the host load was — with guidance written for the stage that actually
aborted — so I can tell contention from a genuine hang without opening the cache entry.

## Context (verified 2026-11-14, TCE `main` @ `70b4981f`)

- `hangTimeoutMessage(elapsedSecs: number)` (`scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts:221`) and
  `listHangMessage(elapsedSecs: number)` (`:237`) print **elapsed** time in the sentence that
  reads as the **bound**; the coverage-preflight fallback (`:492`) already prints the bound.
  Three messages, two shapes, one conflation to remove.
- Both inputs are already in scope at the abort sites: `runVitestProcess` owns `opts.timeoutMs`
  and returns `elapsedSecs`; `runVitestAsync` (`:1214`) and `runVitestListAsync` (`:1246`)
  therefore have bound and elapsed in hand.
- Stage is implicit: `--project unit` / `--project browser` arrive as forwarded argv from
  `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh:92` and `:96`; the pre-flight forwards the same args.
- The browser guidance (`requestAnimationFrame`, undestroyed `Phaser.Game`, run one file under
  `--project browser`) is currently printed for **every** hang, including unit-stage aborts.

## Minimal implementation

- Add one exported `hangDiagnostic(context)` builder taking
  `{ stage, boundMs, elapsedSecs, contention }` and rendering the single shared shape:
  `[hang-timeout] <stage> did not complete within <bound>s — aborting (exit 124)`,
  then `elapsed <n>s (+<delta>s over bound)`, then `host load <l> over <cores> cores`.
- Derive the stage from the forwarded args (`--project <name>`, else `unknown project`); label
  the pre-flight `vitest list (<args>)`. One derivation helper, used by both abort paths.
- Route `runVitestAsync`, `runVitestListAsync` and the coverage-preflight fallback in
  `deriveExpectedFiles` through the builder; drop the `elapsedSecs`-only signatures (no
  backwards-compatible alias — this is an internal script).
- Select guidance by stage: browser block unchanged; unit block points at a synchronous loop in
  test/engine code (`testTimeout` cannot preempt synchronous JS — attach the V8 inspector per
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md`); pre-flight gets the abbreviated form.
- Write the assertions first (rendered content + stage selection), then implement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `[hang-timeout]` abort reports, in the same message: the aborted stage (`--project unit` / `--project browser` / the pre-flight `vitest list`), the configured bound, the elapsed wall time, the delta over the bound, and the host load average at abort plus the core count — so contention is distinguishable from a genuine hang without opening the cache entry. All three hang messages (run abort, pre-flight `vitest list` abort, coverage-preflight fallback) share one builder, so the current elapsed-as-bound wording at `hangTimeoutMessage`/`listHangMessage` is gone and bound, elapsed, stage and load are rendered identically everywhere.
- The hang diagnostic's guidance is stage-appropriate: the browser-stage paragraph (starved `requestAnimationFrame`, undestroyed `Phaser.Game`, run one file under `--project browser`) is **not** printed for a unit-stage abort, which instead points at a synchronous loop in test/engine code.
- The stage label is derived once from the forwarded args and is correct for `--project unit`, `--project browser`, an unrecognised project (rendered as the raw project name, never blank) and the pre-flight `vitest list` path.
- Tests assert the rendered block contains the stage, bound, elapsed, delta, load average and core count, that a browser block contains the `requestAnimationFrame` guidance and a unit block does not (and vice versa), and that no rendered number is labelled as the bound when it is the elapsed time.
- Exit code semantics are untouched: the block still reports exit `124` and still states that no retry is performed.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` — builder, stage derivation, the two abort paths, the coverage-preflight fallback.
- `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` — rendered-content, stage-selection and guidance assertions (extend the existing `hang timeout (bounded wall-clock abort)` block).
- `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` — read-only: confirms the forwarded `--project` args are the stage source.

## Dependencies

- Injectable host contention sampler seam (load average + core count for the block).

## Definition of done

- Tests written first; changed-scope test gate green.
- The `[vitest-runner] attempts=N status=S outcome=hang …` line shape is unchanged.
- ACs evidenced on this item; TCE commit hash + message recorded here.

# Hybrid load-aware unit-stage bound

**Parent:** SA-0MWEURUYL004I470 — Release gate: stage-aware hang diagnostics + hybrid load-aware unit-stage bound
**Slice type:** feature (tracer bullet: bound derivation end-to-end — code, tests, header comment)
**Parent ACs covered:** AC3, AC7

## Goal

As a release producer on a contended host, I want the unit stage's wall-clock bound to grow
with the load the host is actually carrying — from a raised floor up to a finite ceiling — so a
busy machine no longer aborts a green suite at a bound calibrated for an idle one, while a true
hang is still bounded.

## Context (verified 2026-11-14, TCE `main` @ `70b4981f`)

- `DEFAULT_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS = 10 min` (`scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts:188`);
  `parseRunnerArgs` parses `--timeout-ms` at `:322` and it today always wins.
- `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh:92` currently pins the unit bound at `--timeout-ms 300000`, so any
  computed bound would be inert unless the shell stops pinning it (see the wiring child).
- Measured green unit stages: 88, 96, 106, 111, 128, 141, 147, 149, 206, 217 s (worst 217 s =
  72 % of the 300 s bound, 2026-11-11 17:37).
- No load-average awareness exists anywhere in TCE `scripts/` today; `node:os` is already
  imported in the runner.

## Design (decided by this plan; the producer picked "hybrid" at intake, Q1 = C)

- **Static floor** `UNIT_FLOOR_MS = 600_000` (600 s): 2.8× the worst measured green unit stage
  (217 s) and 2× the previous 300 s bound — enough headroom that a merely busy host still
  completes, while a genuinely stuck stage is still aborted.
- **Finite ceiling** `UNIT_CEILING_MS = 1_200_000` (1200 s): equal to the browser bound, and the
  value the outer gate budget is sized against.
- **Load-aware scaling**: `perCore = load1m / cpuCount`;
  `factor = clamp(perCore / 0.75, 1, 2)`; `bound = clamp(floor × factor, floor, ceiling)`.
  At ≤0.75 load/core the floor applies (600 s); at ≥1.5 load/core the ceiling applies
  (1200 s) — e.g. 24 on 16 cores.
- **Override wins verbatim**: an explicit `--timeout-ms` is used as-is with no scaling
  (AC3's "`--timeout-ms` still wins"), so a 4-core CI runner can pin its own number.
- **Portability**: when the sampler reports the load as unavailable (Windows), the floor applies.
- The derivation is a pure exported function so it is testable without spawning anything.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the pure `deriveUnitBound({ floorMs, ceilingMs, load1m, cpuCount, overrideMs })` (name may
  vary) plus the two constants, documented in the file header against the measured baseline.
- Wire it into `parseRunnerArgs`/`main`: absent `--timeout-ms` ⇒ computed bound for `--project
  unit`; explicit `--timeout-ms` ⇒ verbatim. Keep the browser stage's default behaviour as-is
  (no load scaling) so this change is unit-stage-only.
- Pass the same contention sample to the diagnostic so the printed bound is the bound actually
  enforced.
- Write the boundary tests first (idle / loaded / extreme / override / unavailable load), then
  implement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The unit-stage wall-clock bound adopts the operator-approved hybrid strategy: a raised static floor (600 s, justified against the measured baseline — TCE green unit stages observed at 88–217 s against the current 300 s bound) plus load-aware scaling of the bound from the sampled 1-min load average relative to the core count, up to a finite ceiling (1200 s); the bound remains overridable per host (`--timeout-ms`), and `--timeout-ms` still wins over the computed bound.
- The bound derivation is a pure, exported function with the floor and ceiling as explicit constants, so an operator can see the numbers without running a suite; the computed bound never exceeds the finite ceiling and never falls below the static floor for any load value, core count or override.
- Tests cover an idle host (floor applies), a loaded host (scaling applies between floor and ceiling) and an extreme host (ceiling clamps), plus `--timeout-ms` overrides winning verbatim and an unavailable load average (Windows) falling back to the floor; the load average and core count are injected through the test seam and never read from the real host.
- Hang semantics are unchanged: exit `124` (`HANG_TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE`), hangs are never retried, and the `--expect-project-coverage` gate still fails closed on an incomplete run; a bound that cannot fire is not acceptable, so the ceiling is finite and printed in the diagnostic.
- The browser stage's existing bound behaviour is unchanged — the load-aware derivation applies to the unit stage only.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` — constants, pure derivation, `parseRunnerArgs`/`main` wiring, header rationale.
- `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` — floor/scaling/ceiling/override/unavailable-load cases with injected inputs.
- `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` — read-only here; the wiring child changes the invocation.

## Dependencies

- Injectable host contention sampler seam.

## Definition of done

- Boundary tests written first; changed-scope test gate green.
- ACs evidenced on this item; TCE commit hash + message recorded here.

## Goal

As an auditor, I want each cache entry to carry the coarse environment that produced it and the cache key to bind it, so "identical key = identical run" becomes true for the runtime environment as well as for git content.

## Background

Parent SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L, producer decision Q2a: a **coarse, path-independent** environment fingerprint (never the git common dir or the absolute worktree path — that would break the cross-checkout reuse SA-0MWAXZHOU000UBG1 / SA-0MWB1H4RF006R7SI depend on). Cheap and deterministic: no mtimes, no `node_modules` tree hashing, so npm reinstall churn does not produce spurious misses. Depends on the failing tests from `Env-key cache regression tests: drift and equivalence`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `compute_environment_state(cwd)` returns an object with a stable `fingerprint` plus descriptor components: submodule checkout completeness (from `git submodule status`, recording the status prefix + commit per submodule path — repo-relative, never absolute), `node_modules` resolution state (content hash of `node_modules/.package-lock.json` when present; a symlink's *target path is never hashed*, only the installed state it resolves to; missing/empty is a distinct stable marker), and interpreter identity (the resolved pytest executable, machine-level — never a checkout path).
- The computation is cheap (one `git submodule status`, no recursive `node_modules` walk) and deterministic (identical output for an unchanged checkout, stable across innocuous npm reinstall that leaves installed state unchanged).
- `cache_key()` folds `environment_fingerprint` into the key and keeps the historical key **byte-identical** when the argument is omitted (default `""`), so non-git callers and direct unit tests keep working; `store()` persists `environment_fingerprint` + `environment` descriptor in `metadata.json`; `lookup()` compares the caller's fingerprint and treats an entry that predates the field as a miss.
- `run_cached()` / `query_cached()` compute the fingerprint in the checkout they measure/query and thread it through every lookup and store path, including the tree-keyed (`fingerprint_kind="tree"`) namespace.
- An indeterminate environment state (git failure, unreadable marker) is fail-closed: no lookup, no store, fresh execution — consistent with the existing `GitStateUnavailable` behaviour.
- Module docstring and the documented entry layout are updated (new metadata fields, fail-closed rule, legacy entries expire rather than being reinterpreted); new tests from the first child pass and no existing `tests/test_test_cache.py` test regresses.
- Parent AC3 restated — The per-repo test cache key captures a **coarse, path-independent environment fingerprint** — submodule checkout completeness (`git submodule status`), `node_modules` resolution state (symlink target / installed lockfile state), interpreter identity — folded into the fingerprint alongside the existing git/tree state. An in-worktree run and a main-checkout run for the same commit produce distinct entries when their environments differ, and **share** entries when their environments are equivalent (path-independent reuse preserved). The environment fingerprint is computed cheaply and deterministically at lookup and store time, in the consumer's own checkout.

## Minimal implementation

- Add `compute_environment_state()` and a descriptor dataclass/dict in `skill/test_cache.py`, reusing `_run_git()` (repository-override scrubbed) and `resolve_pytest_executable()` from `test_runner`.
- Extend `cache_key()`, `_entry_dir()`, `lookup()`, `store()`, `run_cached()`, `query_cached()` with the fingerprint parameter and metadata comparison; default `""` preserves historical keys.
- Update the module docstring entry-layout block and the `lookup`/`store` docstrings.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/test_cache.py`
- `tests/test_test_cache.py`

## Dependencies

- Depends on: Env-key cache regression tests: drift and equivalence.

## Notes / assumptions

- Coarse proxy assumption (parent): submodule completeness + installed `node_modules` state + interpreter are adequate for reuse decisions.
- Path-independent by construction: only repo-relative submodule paths, the installed-state hash, and the interpreter executable enter the fingerprint.

## Goal

As a build agent, I want the test runner to compute the environment fingerprint in the checkout it actually measures (including the `--gate-commit` subject), so a drifted worktree gate run can never be served as canonical-environment evidence.

## Background

Parent SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L. `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` is the only writer of gate entries: `.githooks/pre-push` runs `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env --gate-commit <sha>` and the finish gate runs `run_tests.py` through `run_gate_suite()` with a tree fingerprint. Both must key on the environment of the resolved subject checkout. Read-only consumers (`--summary`, audit read-only verification) must query with their own checkout's environment fingerprint. Depends on the cache-layer primitive.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every cache lookup/store in `run_tests.py` — full and changed scope, `--gate-commit`, `--fingerprint`, typed/group runs, and `--summary` via `run_summary()` — computes the environment fingerprint in the checkout actually measured (the `--gate-commit` subject resolved by `resolve_gate_subject()`, else `--project-root`, else the detected root) and passes it to `test_cache`.
- A gate run recorded in a drifted worktree is a **miss** for a canonical-checkout query of the same tree (and vice versa is not assumed): the canonical query executes fresh instead of returning green.
- An equivalent-environment gate run at the same tree is reused by a canonical checkout (the existing tree-keyed reuse from `tests/test_pre_push_gate_reuse.py` keeps working).
- The `run_tests.py` result JSON exposes the environment provenance (fingerprint + descriptor components) alongside `git_fingerprint` / `fingerprint_kind` / `interpreter`, so `implement.py finish` and the audit can report it.
- An indeterminate environment fingerprint degrades to a cache bypass (fresh execution, nothing stored) and never to an environment-blind key.
- Tests in `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py` cover equivalent-env reuse and drift-miss for the gate path; existing tests in `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py`, `tests/test_pre_push_gate_reuse.py` and `skill/test/tests/` stay green.
- Parent AC2 restated — A cache-servable invocation in the canonical checkout no longer returns green from an entry recorded in a differently-provisioned worktree without executing: the environment fingerprint part of the key makes such an entry a miss, so the run executes fresh (no silent cache-serve).

## Minimal implementation

- Import `compute_environment_state` into `run_tests.py`; compute once per invocation at the resolved root and thread it through `run_cached`/`query_cached`/`run_summary`.
- Surface `environment` on the result dict and in the `--json` payload; keep the fields additive.
- Update the module/CLI docstrings for `--gate-commit` and `--summary`.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`
- `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py`
- `tests/test_pre_push_gate_reuse.py`

## Dependencies

- Depends on: test_cache environment fingerprint and provenance.

## Notes / assumptions

- The gate's in-place worktree execution model is unchanged (SA-0MVTRBT50005DUEH): only the entry's bindability to canonical-environment evidence changes.

## Goal

Implement `decision_model.py`: the documented, unit-testable reconciliation
rules that turn per-file signals into one `keep` / `rework` / `prune` verdict
with cited evidence — conservative, deterministic and auditable.

## Target outcome

The verdict vertical slice lands: every file receives a verdict whose
justification can be read back, and `prune` is never produced by a lone
heuristic.

## Definition of done

- `DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS` exported with documented values (e.g. mutation healthy
  ≥ 0.60, mutation weak ≤ 0.20, churn rewrite-ratio high ≥ 40 %, churn
  "frequently rewritten" ≥ 4 feature commits) and a `--thresholds <json>`
  override that validates unknown keys loudly.
- `decide(test_file, signals) -> FileVerdict` implementing ordered rules:
  1. A healthy mutation score blocks `prune` outright (behavioural evidence
     outranks a static veto).
  2. `prune` requires ≥ 2 independent prune-leaning signals.
  3. Contradictory keep-lean/prune-lean signals → `rework` + recorded
     conflict.
  4. Cost/stability-only signals (high churn, flaky runtime) → `rework`.
  5. No evidence at all → conservative `keep` flagged `insufficient` per the
     parent's OPEN QUESTION resolution.
- Module docstring documents the signal→stance mapping, the rule ordering and
  the rationale for each threshold.
- The sibling decision-model tests pass unchanged.

## Constraints

- Pure functions over normalised signal objects: no file I/O, no network, no
  subprocess.
- Deterministic: evidence lists are ordered by a fixed signal precedence.
- Advisory only — the model emits a recommendation; nothing deletes a file.
- Every verdict carries ≥ 1 evidence entry or the `insufficient` flag.

## Risky assumptions

- Zero-evidence default is **decided (Option A, producer-confirmed 2026-11-16):** `keep` flagged `insufficient_evidence`, so the three-value totals still reconcile while the report states no evidence exists. See parent item Appendix.
- Threshold values are policy defaults; the model must remain conservative if
  they are retuned (the prune-corroboration rule is threshold-independent).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `decision_model.py` exports `decide()` and `DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS`, with the rule ordering and thresholds documented in the module docstring.
- Emits one verdict per file — `keep`, `rework` or `prune` — with the evidence for that verdict recorded (confidence level plus cited evidence entries).
- A lone static anti-pattern veto can never yield `prune`; a healthy mutation score blocks `prune` regardless of other signals.
- Contradictory signals yield `rework` and record the conflict explicitly.
- An all-signals-absent file yields `keep` with an `insufficient` evidence flag and no invented evidence (Option A, producer-confirmed).
- Threshold override loading validates keys and rejects unknown ones; the sibling decision-model tests pass.

## Key Files

- `skill/test-value/scripts/decision_model.py` — Reconciliation rules, thresholds and verdict type.
- `skill/test-value/tests/test_decision_model.py` — Boundary and case-table tests.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the decision-model test item (test-first).

## Goal

Implement `aggregate_test_value.py`: the single documented entry point that
resolves the project root and in-scope test files, obtains each signal, asks
the decision model for a verdict, and emits `test_value_report.md` +
`test_value_data.json` with reconciled totals and an honest limitations note.

## Target outcome

A producer or agent runs one command and receives the reconciled per-file
keep/rework/prune register plus machine-readable data, with every absent
signal named.

## Definition of done

- CLI: `python3 "$(skill_path test-value)/scripts/aggregate_test_value.py"
  --project-root <path> [--output-dir <path>] [--churn-json …]
  [--mutation-json …] [--suite-source-map …] [--anti-pattern-json …]
  [--runtime-json …] [--thresholds …] [--format {md,json,both}]`.
- Two modes: **orchestrate** (invoke the upstream analysers via
  `skill_path`-resolved paths when no `--*-json` is supplied) and
  **consume** (read pre-generated artefacts, which is what makes runs
  reproducible and testable).
- In-scope test-file set is derived by reusing the existing churn classifier
  (`is_test_file` from `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py`) —
  no second copy of the classification rules.
- `test_value_data.json`: `schema_version`, `generated_at`, pinned-inputs block
  (per-signal status + upstream analyser version), `files[]` (path, verdict,
  confidence, evidence[], conflicts[]), `totals` (keep/rework/prune counts +
  files in scope + `insufficient_evidence` count), `absent_signals[]`,
  `limitations[]`.
- `test_value_report.md`: scope, definitions, per-file register (sorted by
  path), reconciled totals, absent-signals and limitations section, and an
  explicit "prune is advisory — nothing is deleted" statement.
- Totals reconcile: verdict counts sum to files in scope.

## Constraints

- Read-only against the analysed project; never deletes or moves a file.
- No per-project hardcoded paths; project root is an argument.
- Deterministic ordering: files sorted by path, evidence ordered by fixed
  signal precedence, JSON emitted with `sort_keys`.
- Must not duplicate churn/mutation/anti-pattern detection logic — it calls or
  consumes those tools' outputs only.
- Missing inputs degrade honestly: recorded in `absent_signals[]`, reported in
  the limitations note, never back-filled with an inferred value.

## Risky assumptions

- Invoking upstream analysers as subprocesses is the "orchestrate" reading of
  the AC; consuming their JSON is the "reproducible" reading. Supporting both,
  with consume as the tested default, satisfies both without reimplementation.
- Churn per-file coverage is top-20 only, so most files will carry churn
  `absent`; the report must not read as "no churn".

## Acceptance Criteria

- `aggregate_test_value.py` resolves the project root and in-scope test files from arguments only, reusing the existing churn test-file classifier rather than re-implementing it.
- Orchestrates the existing analysers; it does not reimplement churn, mutation or anti-pattern detection — consume mode reads their artefacts, orchestrate mode invokes them, and consume mode is fully exercised by tests.
- Produces `test_value_report.md` + `test_value_data.json` with documented definitions and limitations.
- The report carries scope, definitions, the sorted per-file register, reconciled totals, an absent-signals/limitations section and the explicit advisory-only statement for `prune`.
- `test_value_data.json` contains the documented schema: schema version, pinned-inputs block, per-file verdicts with evidence and conflicts, reconciled totals, absent-signals and limitations.
- Totals reconcile: verdict counts sum to files in scope, and every verdict cites at least one evidence source (or is explicitly flagged `insufficient`).
- Reproducible (pinned inputs, documented command, deterministic ordering) and covered by tests: repeated runs on identical inputs produce identical verdicts and identical report ordering modulo the reported timestamp.

## Key Files

- `skill/test-value/scripts/aggregate_test_value.py` — CLI entry point: scope resolution, signal acquisition, verdict assembly, artefact emission.
- `skill/test-value/scripts/loaders.py` — Signal readers consumed by the entry point.
- `skill/test-value/scripts/decision_model.py` — Verdict rules consumed by the entry point.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the loaders item and the decision-model item.

# Ship Close Marker: Doubled Version Prefix ("Shipped in vv0.1.28")

## Problem

The ship release close path writes close reasons as `Shipped in v${version}`
(`skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`, line ~1111). When `version` carries a
leading `v` (e.g. `v0.1.28`), the resulting close reason becomes
`Shipped in vv0.1.28` — a confusing doubled `v` prefix.

The primary resolution path (line ~2013) already strips the `v` via
`.trim().replace(/^v/, '')`. However, the **fallback path** (reading from
`package.json`, line ~2023) does **not** strip the prefix, leaving the `v`
intact when the git describe call fails.

Observed on SA-0MWE1EAR30045VHO and SA-0MWE4BT63005N8OE (both closed with
`Shipped in vv0.1.28`).

## Users

- Release managers running `skill/ship` — they expect clean, correctly
  formatted close comments on shipped work items.
- Auditors reviewing release history — doubled version prefixes are confusing
  and may signal a broken release process.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The close reason renders `Shipped in vX.Y.Z` exactly once, regardless of
   whether the resolved version carries a `v` prefix.
2. The existing `Shipped in v<version>` marker regex
   (`shippedMarkerPattern`) still matches the close comment for idempotent
   re-close detection (no duplicate closes after the fix).
3. Targeted test covers both a `v`-prefixed and a bare version value.
4. Full project test suite passes.

## Impact

Release close comments show a correctly formatted version instead of a
confusing doubled `v`.

## Constraints

- Cosmetic only; do not change release gating semantics.
- Out of scope: retro-fixing historical close comments.
- The fix should be defensive — applied to the version source so that
  *any* future code path using the version inherits correct formatting.

## Existing State

- `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease(version, ...)` at line ~1111 constructs the
  reason as `` `Shipped in v${version}` ``.
- `version` is resolved from `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` (line ~2010)
  with `.replace(/^v/, '')`, but the package.json fallback (line ~2023) does
  not strip the prefix.
- `shippedMarkerPattern(version)` (line ~569) strips the `v` for regex
  matching, so idempotency checks tolerate either format.

## Desired Change

Strip the leading `v` from the version in the package.json fallback path
(around line 2023), and optionally add a defensive strip at the point where
the version is used in the close reason. This ensures the version is always
bare (e.g. `0.1.28`) before interpolation into `Shipped in v${version}`.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — version resolution (line ~2023),
  close reason construction (line ~1111), and marker regex (line ~569).

## Related Work

- SA-0MWE1EAR30045VHO — observed with `Shipped in vv0.1.28`
- SA-0MWE4BT63005N8OE — observed with `Shipped in vv0.1.28`
- SA-0MUECDK14002J37J — idempotent close-marker implementation (introduced
  `shippedMarkerPattern` and `carriesShippedMarker`)
- SA-0MVX4EHUP0042V9G — Ship skill invalidates audits (parent context)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** The fallback path is rarely exercised (git describe should
  succeed after a release tag is created). Impact of the bug is cosmetic.
- **Risk:** If the fix only targets the fallback path, historical items
  with `vv` markers remain (but this is explicitly out of scope).
- **Assumption:** The `v` prefix in `pkg.version` is non-standard for npm
  projects. The fix should still guard against it defensively.
- **Scope creep:** Do not retro-fix historical close comments.
data.title: Ship close marker renders a doubled version prefix ("Shipped in vv0.1.28")

## Goal

Enforce SA-0MWJ8WGQD0073MG1 AC1/AC3 in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`: `needsProducerReview` is set only when (a) the audit failed for any reason (independent or ship-triggered verdict 'Ready to close: No'), or (b) the audited content/code changed since the last producer review. A passing re-audit of unchanged work — including during a release — never sets it. The ship-triggered carve-out (implemented via SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ) must NEVER swallow the failure signal or the content-change signal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `_resolve_producer_review_decision()` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, ~line 2880) resolves `required` for a top-level failing verdict — independent **and** ship-triggered (the blanket `if ctx.ship_triggered and top_level and verdict in ("yes", "no")` short-circuit at ~line 2943 no longer covers a 'No').
- A passing top-level re-audit of unchanged content (prior passing audit, equal content fingerprint) resolves `preserved` (independent) / `untouched` (ship-triggered) — no flag write in either case.
- A ship-triggered 'Yes' whose stored fingerprint differs from the current content fingerprint resolves `required` (AC3 — marker consulted only after the change signal is evaluated).
- A never-reviewed ship-triggered 'Yes' stays `untouched` (the retained verification carve-out: no prior review baseline means neither AC1 branch holds); the independent equivalent stays `required` (unchanged failsafe).
- Existing carve-outs remain intact and take precedence in their documented order: child items never flagged, cascade-demotion-suppressed 'No' untouched, tainted/infrastructure-failure verdicts untouched, tracked/accepted medium/low candidate-false-positive chores untouched (SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42). Independent-audit behaviour is unchanged apart from these ordered checks (constraint).
- New flag-clearing is NOT introduced on any path: suppression means no write, never `--needs-producer-review no` (SA-0MWJ8WGQD0073MG1 constraints).
- Tests from child SA-0MWJCDH5K002M5H5 pass against the implemented logic; full changed-scope test gate green via the test skill before commit.

### Parent AC coverage (traceability)

- **Covers parent AC1** (SA-0MWJ8WGQD0073MG1): **Producer-review policy is stated and enforced.** `needsProducerReview` is set only when (a) the audit failed for any reason (an independent or ship-triggered verdict of `Ready to close: No`), or (b) the item's audited content/code changed since the last producer review. A passing re-audit of unchanged work — including during a release — never sets it.
- **Covers parent AC3** (SA-0MWJ8WGQD0073MG1): **Code/content-change trigger is not swallowed.** The ship-triggered suppression never overrides the content-fingerprint change signal: a ship-triggered re-audit of an item whose audited content changed since the last review still resolves to `required`, exactly as an independent audit would.

## Minimal Implementation

- Compute the change signal once, before the marker check: `review_stale = bool(prior) and not _producer_review_preserved(wi, prior)` (reusing the existing preserved-review predicate, no new fingerprint logic).
- Replace the blanket ship-triggered short-circuit with a carve-out scoped to the unchanged pass only: suppress when `ctx.ship_triggered and top_level and verdict == "yes" and not review_stale`; return the existing reason string `"ship-triggered audit - flag untouched"`.
- Let a ship-triggered `No` fall through to the existing failing-verdict branch, so the ordered carve-outs still apply (tainted → untouched, cascade-demotion-suppressed → untouched, child → untouched, otherwise `required` with reason `"failing audit (Ready to close: No)"`).
- Let a ship-triggered changed-content `Yes` fall through to the existing passing branch (`_passing_audit_producer_decision` CFP-chore carve-out intact → otherwise `required`).
- Update the `_resolve_producer_review_decision()` docstring truth table (the ship-triggered rows) and the flag-write comment in `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` (~line 17401) to state the only-when-failed-or-changed rule and the marker boundary.
- Keep the decision resolved once before persistence and reused by the lifecycle write, so the recorded `Producer review: required|preserved|untouched (<reason>)` line can never disagree with the flag write.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_resolve_producer_review_decision()` (~line 2880), `_passing_audit_producer_decision()` (~line 2674), `_producer_review_preserved()`, `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()` flag write (~line 17401), `--ship-triggered` parser (~line 18600).

## Dependencies

- SA-0MWJCDH5K002M5H5 (test-first; the tests define the expected boundary).
- SA-0MWJ7K962006646G (`--ship-triggered` marker wiring — completed; this item constrains how the marker is consulted).

## Deliverables

- Runner logic enforcing only-when-failed-or-changed; changed-scope tests green.

- **Producer-review policy is stated and enforced.** `needsProducerReview` is set only when (a) the audit failed for any reason (an independent or ship-triggered verdict of `Ready to close: No`), or (b) the item's audited content/code changed since the last producer review. A passing re-audit of unchanged work - including during a release - never sets it.
- **Code/content-change trigger is not swallowed.** The ship-triggered suppression never overrides the content-fingerprint change signal: a ship-triggered re-audit of an item whose audited content changed since the last review still resolves to `required`, exactly as an independent audit would.

## Summary

Fix `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria()` so section
detection and section exit use one consistent, **heading-level-relative** rule,
and pin it with regression tests written first inside this item (TDD).

Root cause: detection matches any heading level
(`^#+\s+Acceptance\s+Criteria`) but exit breaks only on H2 (`^##\s+`); the later
any-heading branch merely flushes the open entry and continues, so bullets
under a sibling `# Key Files` / `# Related work` heading are collected as ACs
and the coverage review reports them as uncovered.

## Normative rule (agreed with the producer, Option B)

1. Detection captures the AC heading level: `^(#{1,6})\s+Acceptance\s+Criteria`.
2. Inside the section, a heading line `^(#{1,6})\s+` with level **≤** the
   captured level ends the section.
3. A heading **deeper** than the captured level flushes the open AC entry and is
   otherwise ignored (existing behaviour preserved).
4. An unparseable/absent captured level falls back to breaking on level ≤ 2.
5. Fenced code blocks, markdown tables, lone list markers and blank-line
   boundaries are unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `extract_acceptance_criteria()` stops collecting AC bullets at the next heading whose level is the same or higher than the AC section heading (levels 1–6), and a deeper heading stays inside the section.
- An H1-headed description whose `# Key Files` and `# Related work` bullets follow `# Acceptance Criteria` returns exactly the AC bullets — no file paths, no related-work entries.
- A `### Acceptance Criteria` section terminated by a sibling `### Key Files` heading stops there, proving the rule is level-relative rather than hard-coded to H1/H2.
- `## Acceptance Criteria` followed by `### Notes` and a bullet still collects that bullet, so `test_heading_inside_ac_section_not_appended` passes unmodified.
- Existing H2-headed parsing tests remain green: `test_stops_at_next_heading`, `test_simple_acs` and the other pre-existing H2 fixtures pass unmodified.
- One test is named for this item's ID (`SA-0MUKCQ4TL0075WZJ`) so the regression is traceable from the suite, and `run_coverage_review` returns `proceed` for an H1-headed parent fixture rather than `stop`.
- The module-level "AC-coverage similarity semantics" docstring, the `extract_acceptance_criteria()` docstring, and the AC-format bullet in `skill/plan/SKILL.md` all describe the same-or-higher termination rule that the code implements.

## Minimal Implementation

- Write the failing regression tests first (H1 sibling leak, H3 section + `### Key Files` sibling, H2 + `### Notes` retained, H2 + `## Constraints` retained, `run_coverage_review` proceeds), then make them pass in the same item so the suite is never left red.
- Capture the AC heading level at detection time; keep it in a local variable alongside `in_ac_section`.
- Replace the `^##\s+` break with a level comparison against the captured level; fold the now-redundant deeper-heading branch into that single check so the function has exactly one heading rule.
- Update the two docstrings and the `skill/plan/SKILL.md` "AC list formats" bullet; do not touch `has_acceptance_criteria_section()` (presence detection is level-agnostic by design).
- No new dependencies; no behaviour change for descriptions whose sections are all H2.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py`
- `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py`
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md`

## Related work

- child-of: SA-0MUKCQ4TL0075WZJ
- rule-agreed-in: SA-C0MWKJBJUP002RO05 (producer chose Option B)
- absorbed: SA-0MWKJCYJK00430Z8 (a test-only child could not reach a green finish gate; tests and fix are one vertical slice)
- blocks: SA-0MWKJDK8G009ON4T (audit parity)

## Impact

Users planning work items written with H1 or H3 headings no longer see their Key Files paths and related-work links reported as uncovered acceptance criteria.

## Summary

Author the failing-first regression tests that pin the desired behaviour: `implement.py start` resumes an item's **existing** worktree and branch even when the work item's current title slug differs from the slug used when the worktree was created (SA-0MVXUHAM3006BRNC AC1–AC4).

New module: `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_slug_drift.py`, following the real-git-repo fixture style of `test_phase_start_resume_from_worktree.py`. `_get_repo_root`, `_discover_worktree`, `worktree_path_for` and `branch_name_for` are deliberately **not** mocked — that mocking is exactly why the sibling defect SA-0MVXUGXS5006M3HF escaped coverage.

## Why this item comes first

Test-first ordering: these tests are authored before the fix so the fix is provably driven by them. Until the fix lands, the tests are marked `@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="SA-0MVXUHAM3006BRNC not fixed yet")`, which keeps the suite green and makes the marker removal in the implementation child a genuine TDD signal (a `strict` xfail fails as soon as the behaviour becomes correct).

## Scenarios

1. **AC1 — resume from the main checkout.** Real temp git repo, canonical worktree and branch created for slug A (`wl-<id>-<slug-a>`); `wl_show` now returns a title whose slug is B; `phase_start` runs from the main checkout. Assert `resumed is True`, `report["worktree_path"]` is the existing tree, `git_worktree_add` is never called, exactly one directory matches `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-*`, and no second branch `wl-<id>-<slug-b>` exists (`git branch --list`).
2. **AC2 — resume from inside the existing worktree.** Same setup with `cwd` = the old-slug worktree; same assertions, plus no `<worktree>/.worklog/worktrees/…` path is created.
3. **AC3 — fresh start unchanged.** No worktree exists and the title is unchanged: `resumed is False`, the tree is created at `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`, branch `wl-<id>-<slug>`.
4. **Already-broken case.** Two worktrees exist for the item (old slug + new slug — the defect's symptom): the tree carrying `.implement_state.json` wins, the run resumes it, and the report names both the chosen and the ignored candidate.
5. **Branch fidelity.** The resumed report's `branch` is the branch actually checked out in the existing worktree, not the slug-derived name.

## Minimal implementation

- Reuse the `_patch_externals`-style context manager pattern from `test_phase_start_resume_from_worktree.py`; hoist a shared helper for "create the worktree for slug X".
- Assert on observable state (report fields, `git branch --list`, directory scan, `git_worktree_add` calls), never on private call shapes.
- Mark the five scenarios `xfail(strict=True)` with the reason string naming this item's fix child.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_slug_drift.py` exists and covers scenarios 1–5, each with a real temporary git repository plus a linked worktree (AC4).
- Every test asserts the observable contract — one worktree only, no new branch, and the `resumed` / `worktree_path` / `branch` report fields — rather than internal call shapes.
- The tests do not mock `_get_repo_root`, `_discover_worktree`, `worktree_path_for` or `branch_name_for`.
- With the fix absent, the new module reports the five scenarios as `xfail`ed (never as errors) and the changed-scope suite is green.
- Removing the `xfail` markers on the un-fixed code makes every scenario fail (the test genuinely pins the defect).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_slug_drift.py` (new)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_resume_from_worktree.py` (fixture and patch-harness pattern to follow)

## Dependencies

None — created first; the implementation child depends on this one.

## Deliverables

- The regression test module, plus the changed-scope test evidence recorded on this item.

## Impact

The slug-drift defect is pinned by executable tests before the fix, so a title edit can never silently reintroduce a duplicate worktree.

## Goal

Pin the spawn-failure classifier's vocabulary and fail-safe **before** any retry code exists, so the drive loop can only ever retry a genuine provider/model-resolution failure.

User story: As an implement-skill maintainer, I want the spawn-failure classification to be table-driven and tested first, so extending the infrastructure-retry budget to spawn-time failures can never silently retry a real defect.

## Context

`CUR-0MWL0EBP30071E1J` (games_curator) reports driven child sessions dying at startup with `No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"` and aborting the drive chain. Upstream plan: features F1–F3 + F5 live in this repository; the config half is folded into `SA-0MWL5AL4B004X0FN`. This item is **F1 — test-first**.

Findings from the planning session (code-grounded):

- `_default_session_spawner` reports a non-zero exit as `Child session for <id> exited with code N: <5-line tail>` — the provider text arrives **inside `reason`**.
- `_pane_session_spawner` reports `Failed to start the pane agent for <id>: …` or `Pane agent for <id> did not complete: …`.
- `classify_finish_failure` + `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS` is the existing table-driven infra vocabulary, but it is **finish-only**; there is no spawn-side classifier.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `classify_spawn_failure(reason)` helper exists in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` returning `{kind, reason, provider, remedy}` and is driven by an explicit allow-list table (mirroring `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS`), never by prose sniffing in `phase_drive`.
- Tests (written first, failing before the helper exists) assert: a headless `Child session for X exited with code 1: … No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"` reason classifies as `kind == "infrastructure"` with `provider == "MunitoAI"` and a non-empty remedy.
- The pane flavours (`Failed to start the pane agent for X: …` and `Pane agent for X did not complete: …`) carrying the same provider text classify as `infrastructure`.
- Fail-safe is pinned: an unclassified reason (a Python traceback tail, an arbitrary message, an empty string, `None`) classifies as `kind == "unknown"` — never `infrastructure`.
- A `timed out` reason is not reclassified as provider-infrastructure (the timeout path keeps its own reconciliation semantics).
- The remedy text names the concrete action (drop the unservable pattern from `enabledModels`, or provide the missing API key) and is asserted by at least one test.

# Test-first contract: intake preserves refactor identity markers

## Summary

Define, as failing-first tests, the contract that intake's draft application step preserves the `Refactor-Finding-Key:`, `Refactor-Fingerprint:` and `Refactor-Affected-Lines:` lines already present in a refactor item's description — before the implementation in the sibling feature lands. Parent: `SA-0MWL5PKM5005QS9C` AC1, AC2, AC5.

## Test-first convention

Matches the existing repo precedent (`SA-0MWE1DXPW00846UV`, `tests/test_refactor/test_dedupe_identity.py`): tests are written first and each test probes for the *specific* helper/constant the implementation feature introduces. A test whose helper has not landed yet skips with an explicit `not yet implemented (SA-<impl-id>)` reason, so this item's changed-scope gate stays green while the implementation item is still open, and the implementation item's gate turns the same tests green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New test module `skill/intake/tests/test_intake_marker_preservation.py` exists and is collected by the project test runner.
- The module defines tests for all four marker-preservation scenarios: (a) markers present in the current description are present in the applied description, (b) an item with no markers gains none, (c) re-running the merge is idempotent (no duplicated marker lines), (d) a non-refactor item's description is byte-identical after the merge.
- Additional cases are covered: marker preservation when the draft has no leading `#`/`##` heading (markers go to the very top), and markers embedded mid-line (quoted inside prose) are **not** preserved.
- Assertions compare exact marker lines (`Refactor-Finding-Key: <code>:<path>` etc.) and assert the preserved block sits before the draft's first `##` heading, not merely "somewhere in the text".
- Each test that requires a not-yet-landed helper calls `pytest.skip("<reason> (SA-<impl-id>)")` via an import-capability guard, so the module passes on its own before the implementation exists.
- `python3 skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py --scope changed` (via the test skill) passes.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the new test module following the style of `skill/intake/tests/test_intake_scripts_cwd.py` (repo-root `sys.path` insertion, `mock.patch` of `shared.status_lifecycle._find_worklog_dir_by_prefix` for hermetic worklog resolution, `mock.patch` of `intake.scripts.intake.run_wl` to capture the `wl update` invocation).
- Provide a small local fixture factory that writes a draft markdown file to `tmp_path` and a fake `wl show <id> --json` payload for the current description.

## Key Files

- `skill/intake/tests/test_intake_marker_preservation.py` — new contract test module (all preservation cases).
- `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` — read-only reference for the `cmd_finish` / `_run_wl_update_description` seams the tests target.
- `skill/intake/tests/test_intake_scripts_cwd.py` — style/mocking reference.

## Constraints

- No production code changes in this item — tests only.
- Tests must not shell out to a real `wl` store; the store is mocked or a `tmp_path` worklog is used.
- Follow `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`: no self-referential simulations, no duplicates of existing coverage.

## Dependencies

None — created first (test-first ordering).

## Summary

Define, as failing-first tests, the contract that the refactor pre-creation duplicate guard recognises a non-terminal **marker-less legacy** refactor item by reconstructing its `<code>:<repository-relative path>` identity from its title/description. This is the damage-repair half: items already rewritten by intake cannot regain markers, so they must still suppress duplicate filings. Parent: `SA-0MWL5PKM5005QS9C` AC3, AC4, AC5.

## Test-first convention

Extends `tests/test_refactor/test_dedupe_identity.py` in the established style: each test probes for the specific helper the implementation feature introduces and skips with `not yet implemented (SA-0MWLLKNJU0015592)` while that helper is absent, so this item's changed-scope gate is green before the implementation lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/test_refactor/test_dedupe_identity.py` gains a legacy-fallback section covering a **match**: a non-terminal, marker-less item whose description carries structured `- **Code:** \`S112\`` and `- **File:** \`skill/x.py\`` fields is returned by the duplicate guard for the smell `S112` in `skill/x.py`.
